documentation: Math.round returns the nearest integer. An exact halfway value rounds toward positive infinity, so 2.5 becomes 3 while -2.5 becomes -2. Values between -0.5 and zero can produce negative zero.
inputs: An array of finite numbers with magnitude below one million.
returns: Nearest integers, with zero represented as ordinary JSON zero.
caution: This is not the same tie rule as Python round or rounding halfway away from zero. Floating-point decimal arithmetic can introduce representation error; this exercise rounds supplied values directly.
scenarios: Snap a drag position to an integer grid coordinate.
Display a measured duration as a nearest whole second.
Assign an approximate distance to its nearest whole-unit bucket.
title: Round signed measurements
problem: Round each finite input number with JavaScript Math.round semantics. Treat negative zero and zero as the same JSON result. Preserve order.
hint: Halfway values go toward positive infinity, including negative inputs.
goal: Use Math.round() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
